question: Does the frozen rank48 OOD circuit remain predictive when its cue-source embedding displacement is corrupted by isotropic noise?
intervention: On temporal-v12/iswas-v11 targets and temporal-v12 P controls, replace the changed cue embedding by the donor embedding plus Gaussian noise whose per-row RMS is exactly 10% of the recipient-to-donor embedding displacement RMS. Use seeds 1729, 2718, and 3141; all support, readers, and actuation remain frozen.

predictions.pred_a_authority_noise_tripwire_finitene: authorities replay, support has 48 sites, every noise RMS ratio is in [0.099,0.101], values are finite, and <=34 forwards execute
predictions.pred_b_noisy_ood_coordinates_transfer: for every seed and fit all coordinate projections are >=0.70 and mean residual <=0.25
predictions.pred_c_noisy_ood_behavior_transfer: for every seed and fit both task projections are >=0.75 and worst target residual <=0.20
predictions.pred_d_noisy_ood_controls_are_selective: all controls have margin RMS <=0.10, median full-vocabulary KL <=0.02, and flip fraction <=0.05
predictions.pred_e_noise_seed_stability: the range across seeds of minimum coordinate projection and each task projection is <=0.08 within each fit

decision: Passing establishes end-to-end source perturbation robustness in addition to clean lexical OOD transfer. Failure localizes whether noise breaks upstream coordinate writing or only the downstream behavioral map; it does not trigger refitting.
